literature_status: Nonsplit sixfold Weil classes remain unresolved in the same-day reviewed sources; no exhaustive global status or nonalgebraicity asserted. Markman split-sixfold theorem does not cover discriminant -3.

geometry.lattice: Z[i]^6 in C^6, ordered real coordinates (x1,y1,...,x6,y6)
geometry.positive_plane: W={(v,Zv):v in C^3}; h-positive since I-Z*diag(1,1,3)Z is positive definite
geometry.complex_structure: J=i on W and -i on W_perp; equivalently J=A diag(iI3,-iI3) A^-1, A=[[I3,Z*diag(1,1,3)],[Z,I3]]
geometry.X: (C^6 as a real vector space with complex structure J)/Z[i]^6
geometry.projectivity: E is integral, J-compatible and E(v,Jv)>0. The imported Riemann criterion gives a polarized projective abelian sixfold.

class.nonzero_period: integral over the real x-coordinate six-torus is 1

genericity: The 18 real coordinates are algebraically independent over Q by Q-linear independence of distinct prime square roots and Lindemann-Weierstrass. Rational Hodge conditions expressed polynomially in these period coordinates cannot hold accidentally.

picard_certificate.sample_rule: Z=0 and Z with just one entry equal to 1/8 or i/8; 19 marked rational period samples
picard_certificate.constraint: (wedge^2 J*)v=v; algebraic independence transports any rational (1,1) class at the selected point to every sample
picard_certificate.conclusion: NS(X)_Q=Q E by Lefschetz (1,1). Divisor products in degree six span Q E^3. Alpha is not in this span.
